answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a refundable deposit that grows with the number of identities it controls, like a lotus that opens only one bloom per root. Newcomers start with tiny earning caps and must build a verifiable work history before their votes count, so an attacker facing a rising tide of fake accounts finds each new identity costs real money and time while yielding almost nothing. The old fable of the hydra applies: cut off one head and two grow, unless every head must pay to exist, in which case spawning heads bankrupts the attacker first.
